beats.say: Coding agents read code like text. Ask Claude Code who uses Approval Required Tool, and it searches, opens a thousand-line file, searches again, and it's still reading.
repo-analysis fixes this underneath the agent. It parses the codebase once into a code graph, with Rust in depth through rust analyzer, and serves it to any agent as sixteen MCP tools.
Same question, with the tools. Find symbol locates the struct. Symbol relations returns its exact callers, across crates. The answer comes from the graph, not from guessing.
Spelunk puts that same graph in front of the whole team.
When the room talks about code, Spelunk listens. Resonate transcribes the conversation live, and tells the speakers apart.
Claude Haiku reads each new sentence and grounds it in the real code, calling the same MCP tools.
Then it acts. A change someone suggests becomes a proposal, pinned to the node it touches. A question asked in the room gets an answer, straight from the code.
Nothing moves without a yes. The team accepts one proposal, and declines the other.
Accepted decisions become a handoff document, saved on the MCP server, where any connected coding agent can pick it up.
The repo ships a Claude Code skill for exactly this: spelunk handoff.
Claude Code pulls the handoff: what was decided, who said it, and where it lives in the code. It makes the change, asks before it runs the tests, and marks the handoff done.
Talk it through. Decide together. Let the agent build it. That's Spelunk.
